decisions.reason: Confirmed nonfatal representative ambiguity: the quoted L2 definition makes g an equivalence class, while kernel evaluation requires a representative. Fixed a finite real measurable representative explicitly; invariance gives pi(P1_A)=0 for every pi-null A, proving the evaluations and both kernel integrals are independent of this choice almost surely. The truncation, conditional Jensen, martingale-difference and variance-expansion arguments are valid. Also removed the in-step self-reference and replaced Borel by measurable on the arbitrary state space.

Confirmed fatal dependency-citation gap: the definition requires a measurable isomorphism to an entire Polish space, and the cited corollary establishes only G-delta subspaces, not arbitrary Borel subspaces. Repaired without changing the Statement: keep S equal to the closed Cantor space, retain the original kernel on the absorbing full Borel set B, and send every exceptional state directly to pi_c. The envelope and observation are zero off B, giving the all-state bound there; initial and stationary laws are supported on B. For lifting only the real sequence space is needed, which is a countable product of Polish real lines. No arbitrary-Borel-subspace theorem remains in the proof.

False positive: the title names the subject without quantifying over dimensions; the formal Statement explicitly requires 1<=d<=2 and the proof uses joint parent/bridge dimension 2d<=4. The dependent quantile supplier covers precisely that dimension range. Checked the Bernstein estimate, half-Gaussian anchors, stopped dyadic interpolation, short-row branch, product marginals and successive target-row replacement. In step 6.1 the retained Gaussian subsequence is the output mixed marginal, as its following product-law sentence states; its errors telescope by step 7.1. There is no claimed theorem for arbitrary dimension and no item edit is warranted.

Confirmed fatal logic gap in step 8.1: the old Gaussian odd coordinates can depend on the newly generated raw evens, since the root/split transport reads the whole old row. Their independence is not supplied by F7. Repaired by replacing the entire active row by the mixed target, freezing target evens and retaining target Gaussian odds. F7 separates that entire target from the old frozen complement; the target product law separates its own odd and even coordinates. Step 9.1 now defines full intermediate rows and telescopes their differences, including Gaussian-odd changes, against the saved initial Gaussian row. Checked the noncommuting covariance interpolation, positive anchor fraction, explicit terminal posterior, moderate-region concentration, short-row branch and parameterwise measurability; the Statement is unchanged.
